Duties to include but are not limited to: Responsible for providing competent, evidence-based care to primary care patients and oversight of licensed vocational nurses/nursing assistants, as appropriate to the setting. Manages assigned panel(s), utilizes registries, and ensures appropriate evaluation and access is provided to patient panels.

Provides health promotion, health education and coaching on wellness, disease prevention, and chronic care management. Administers medications and procedures per established policies and guidelines. Influences care outcomes by collaborating with members of the interdisciplinary team.

Assists in directing the provision of nursing education, orientation, competencies and providing quality improvement and outcomes utilization. Applies clinical knowledge/judgment to lead staff involvement in planning, decision-making, and evaluating outcomes within the immediate practice setting.

Improves Veteran/patient driven care by resolving experience issues such as coordination of care, timeliness or process issues, common themes of dissatisfaction, or environment of care concerns for the immediate practice setting.

Graduate of a school of professional nursing approved by the appropriate accrediting agency and accredited by one of the following accrediting bodies at the time the program was completed by the applicant: The Accreditation Commission for Education in Nursing (ACEN) or The Commission on Collegiate Nursing Education (CCNE); OR Individuals attending a master's level bridge program in nursing who have completed coursework equivalent to a bachelor's level degree in Nursing may have opportunity to become registered as a nurse with a state licensing board prior to completion of the bridge program.

(Reference VA Handbook 5005, Appendix G6); OR In cases of graduates of foreign schools of professional nursing, possession of a current, full, active, and unrestricted registration will meet the requirement for graduation from an approved school of professional nursing to warrant an appointment as a Nurse who has completed an associated degree/entry level Nursing education program.

The Cath Lab RN is responsible for delivering safe, patient-centered care throughout the continuum of the procedure, including pre-procedure assessment, intra-procedure monitoring, moderate sedation management (as applicable), post-procedure recovery, and patient education.

The nurse promotes quality outcomes through adherence to VA standards, evidence-based practice, and continuous quality improvement initiatives. Major Duties and Responsibilities: Perform comprehensive nursing assessments before, during, and after cardiac catheterization and electrophysiology procedures.

Provide care for Veterans undergoing diagnostic and interventional procedures, including coronary angiography, percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), peripheral vascular interventions, structural heart procedures, and electrophysiology studies.

Continuously monitor cardiac rhythms, hemodynamic status, oxygenation, and patient response throughout procedures. Administer and monitor moderate sedation and emergency medications in accordance with VA policies and nursing standards.

Recognize and respond rapidly to cardiac emergencies, including arrhythmias, hemodynamic instability, myocardial infarction, cardiac arrest, and procedural complications. Assist physicians during invasive cardiovascular procedures by maintaining sterile technique and ensuring availability of specialized equipment and supplies.

Operate and troubleshoot specialized Cath Lab equipment including hemodynamic monitoring systems, contrast injectors, and emergency resuscitation equipment. Recover patients following procedures, monitor vascular access sites, identify complications, and provide discharge education.

Educate Veterans and caregivers regarding procedures, medications, recovery expectations, risk factor modification, and follow-up care. Collaborate with cardiologists, electrophysiologists, radiologic technologists, cardiovascular technologists, anesthesia providers, pharmacists, and other interdisciplinary team members.

Participate in STEMI activations and emergency cardiac interventions, including after-hours call responsibilities as assigned by the facility. Ensure compliance with infection prevention standards, radiation safety practices, and procedural safety protocols.

Participate in quality improvement initiatives, performance metrics, competency validation, and evidence-based practice projects. Serve as a clinical resource, mentor, and preceptor for nursing staff and students as appropriate. Maintain accurate and timely documentation within the VA electronic health record.

Promote a culture of safety, Veteran-centered care, professionalism, and continuous learning.

Surgical Services include: Cardiovascular, Thoracic, Transplant, Peripheral Vascular, Neurosurgical, Orthopedic, General Surgery, Urology, ENT and Plastics.

Additional conditions include myocardial infarction, unstable angina/arrhythmias, post PTCA, pacemaker placement, subdural hematoma, post-op cardiothoracic surgery, pre/post heart/liver/lung transplant, LVAD implant, post arrest hypothermia, carotid artery and femoral popliteal bypass surgery.

Nursing care is provided on a 24-hour basis by registered nurses and nursing assistants. The nursing process of assessment, planning, implementation and evaluation is applied in an ongoing, systematic manner to all patients.

The ICU provides acute level nursing and RNs are intricately involved in the development, implementation, and evaluation of interdisciplinary care.

This requires nursing staff to participate with an interdisciplinary approach in meeting Veteran health care needs, including being an active participant in Interdisciplinary rounds consisting of the entire team of Physicians, Nurse Practitioners, Nutrition Service/Dietician, Physical Therapy, Occupational Therapy, Social Work, Pharmacy, and other specialty groups as needed; coordinating care of all patients.

This systematic process is applied to all patients with a goal of care to restore the Veteran to maximum function, prevent further decline, maximize independence, and/or provide comfort as necessary.

Discharge planning is an essential component of our nursing practice and an interdisciplinary approach for teaching and discharge planning assures continuity of care for the Veterans we serve. RNs respond to Code Blue emergencies and inpatient Rapid Response Calls and recover patients directly from the OR on off tours.

RNs are required to complete the basic critical care course and/or successfully pass a competency exam (Basic Knowledge Assessment Test). Each RN must complete a period of supervised practice in the ICU.

The length of the orientation will be individualized based on assessments of the new employee's experience and nursing education as well as preceptor and nurse manager's evaluations. No nurse assumes full patient care responsibility or functions as charge nurse until authorized by the nurse manager and completion of the charge nurse classes.

Registered Nurse (Germany) – Remote About Us Think Global - Expect Amazing! TalentWorldGroup is a revolutionary multilingual Contact Center. We are a truly people-focused company on a mission to reinvent professional home-based working and build the Workplace of the Future.

Position Overview We are currently qualifying candidates for an upcoming remote Registered Nurse project scheduled to start at the end of Summer / beginning of Fall. We are seeking Registered Nurses located in Germany with an active German RN license to support one of our premium international clients in the medical field.

This is a fully remote, work-from-home opportunity where you will provide professional support to patients and healthcare professionals following a comprehensive paid training program. Key Responsibilities
Resolve customer inquiries, complaints, and requests, including technical or clinical information while working within a defined scope of practice.
Serve as a telecare clinical contact for patients, clinical staff, and internal team members.
Support escalations from the Level 1 Technical Services team when required.
Follow all environmental, health, and safety procedures and company policies.
Act as a liaison between customers, TalentWorldGroup, and the client.
Help maintain the accuracy of online knowledge bases, troubleshooting guides, and reference materials.
Identify opportunities to improve customer experience, equipment reliability, and treatment quality.
Complete scheduled and unscheduled outbound calls to telecare patients and clinical collaborators.
Receive inbound calls from telecare patients and clinical collaborators.
Analyze treatment data and identify clinical, user, or product-related trends.
Document all interactions accurately and share relevant information with appropriate stakeholders.
Training Program
8 weeks of paid remote training
Covers technical support, systems, and treatment analysis.
Training Schedule: Monday to Friday, 4:00 PM – 10:00 PM CEST (6 hours training)- ﻿For six weeks with a two weeks nesting period
Working Schedule
Operating Hours: Monday to Friday, between 9:00 AM and 6:00 PM CET
Expected workload: Approximately 2 hours per day
Fully remote from Germany

€26/hour during training
€28/hour after successful completion of training

Currently living in Germany
Active Registered Nurse (RN) license issued in Germany
Nursing degree (BSc or equivalent nursing diploma)
Excellent verbal and written communication skills in German and English
2–4 years of customer service or contact center experience is preferred but not required
Experience with dialysis therapy is an advantage but not mandatory

Broadband internet connection (Ethernet/LAN, minimum 50 Mbps)
Intel Core i5 / AMD Ryzen 5 or higher

The Nurse Educator role collaborates with nursing leadership, interdisciplinary teams, and academic partners to identify learning needs, support orientation and competency programs, and improve patient outcomes across the healthcare system.

Duties and Responsibilities include but limited to: Assess learning and competency needs of nursing staff through performance data, observations, regulatory requirements, and collaboration with leadership. Design, develop, implement, and evaluate evidence-based educational programs, in-services, and continuing education activities.

Provide clinical instruction, training, and consultation for nurses and other healthcare staff in inpatient and outpatient settings. Coordinate orientation programs for newly hired nurses and clinical staff and evaluate their progress during onboarding. Develop individualized learning plans to address identified performance or competency gaps.

Conduct competency assessments, skills validations, return demonstrations, and performance evaluations. Serve as a mentor, coach, preceptor, and role model for nursing staff, students, residents, and interdisciplinary team members.

Support nurse residency programs and facilitate educational activities using simulation, case studies, lectures, and other adult learning methodologies. Serve as a trainer and consultant for the Resuscitation Education Initiative (REDI) and maintain certification as a Basic Life Support (BLS) instructor when required.

Monitor and track BLS, ACLS, and other mandatory certification compliance for staff. Organize, facilitate, and evaluate mock codes, emergency preparedness drills, and resuscitation training programs. Collaborate with interdisciplinary teams to improve quality, patient safety, and clinical outcomes.

Promote evidence-based practice by reviewing current literature, identifying best practices, and recommending changes to clinical practice and documentation. Assist with accreditation readiness and ensure compliance with VA, Joint Commission, and regulatory standards.

Analyze educational outcomes and competency data to evaluate program effectiveness and support performance improvement initiatives. Participate in committees, workgroups, and organizational initiatives that support nursing excellence and Veteran care.

## Description de l'entreprise ##
Avec plus de 13'000 collaborateurs et collaboratrices représentant 160 métiers, les Hôpitaux Universitaires de Genève sont un établissement de référence au niveau national et international. Pour en savoir plus sur notre institution, prenez quelques minutes pour consulter notre rétrospective 2025 en cliquant ici.
Le poste est rattaché au Département de la femme, de l'enfant et de l'adolescent qui a pour mission d-offrir des soins de qualité et adaptés aux besoins des femmes à chaque étape de leur vie et aux problèmes de santé auxquels sont confrontés les nouveau-nés, les enfants et les adolescentes et adolescents de leur naissance jusqu'à l'âge de 16 ans. Il œuvre au développement des prestations de pointe et des pôles de compétence de spécialité.
Le Service de Soins intensifs de néonatologie et de soins intensifs de pédiatriques prend en charge, tout nouveau-né, nourrisson ou enfant dont les fonctions vitales sont menacées et qui nécessite une surveillance ou un geste thérapeutique relevant de la médecine intensive.
Les équipes soutiennent la patientèle et leurs proches dans ces situations de crise, afin d-entreprendre tout ce qui est nécessaire et possible pour améliorer la qualité de vie et la survie des enfants dont l-état nécessite une surveillance ou un traitement spécialisé.
## Description du poste ##
En tant qu-infirmier ou infirmière spécialisée en soins intensifs de néonatologie et pédiatriques, vous dispensez de manière autonome et/ou sur délégation médicale, des soins infirmiers spécialisés et globaux à tout nouveau-né, enfant ou adolescent ou adolescente et dans des situations présentant différents niveaux de complexité.
Vous intégrez les parents dans la prise en soins de leur enfant et les considérez comme des partenaires avec un accompagnement adapté. Travailler avec des enfants prématurés en soutenant les parents dans ce moment de vie particulier sera votre quotidien.
Vous travaillez dans les unités de soins intensifs de néonatologie et pédiatriques et collaborez activement à l-encadrement et l-enseignement du nouveau personnel soignant, des étudiantes ou étudiants et d-autres professionnelles ou professionnels de la santé.
Grâce à votre professionnalisme, vous contribuez au développement de la qualité des soins et à la recherche dans le domaine de la santé.

Vous êtes en possession d'un Bachelor HES en soins infirmiers, ou d'un diplôme en soins infirmiers reconnu par la Croix-Rouge suisse.
Vous êtes titulaire du diplôme d-expert ou d'experte en soins intensifs EPD-ES, ou êtes prêt ou prête à effectuer cette formation aux HUG (cf. ci-dessous).
Les atouts seront : une expérience dans un service de Néonatologie niveau 2/3 ; une formation certifiante en pédiatrie (DAS SEAF ou équivalent), une expérience en soins aigus pédiatriques.
Vous avez d'excellentes qualités relationnelles, vous aimez le travail en équipe et vous vous intégrez facilement dans de nouveaux environnements professionnels. Votre autonomie, votre rigueur et votre capacité à prioriser font de vous un ou une professionnelle précise dans l'exécution des tâches et responsabilités qui vous sont confiées.
Vous avez d'excellentes capacités à gérer les environnements stressants tout en faisant preuve de réactivité. Votre entourage professionnel vous reconnait des qualités relationnelles, une aptitude à prendre du recul et un sens de la communication développé.
Vous avez une appétence pour le domaine de l-accompagnement aux proches particulièrement le soutien à la parentalité. Vous avez le projet de développer des compétences dans le domaine pédiatrique.
Si vous vous reconnaissez dans ce profil, n-hésitez pas à nous envoyer votre candidature. Après une première analyse de votre dossier, s-il est retenu, vous serez invité ou invitée à réaliser un diagnostic de vos connaissances théoriques.
Pour cela, vous recevrez par mail un lien vers un MOOC en ligne qui vous permettra d-auto-évaluer votre socle de connaissances théoriques. Cette évaluation des compétences est une formation en ligne qui vous demandera un investissement de plusieurs heures (compter environ 10 heures de formation) et qui vous invite à vous plonger dans la réalité des services spécialisés en vous proposant des auto-évaluations et des supports didactiques vous permettant de développer vos compétences.
Une fois que vous aurez réalisé le MOOC dans son intégralité, votre diagnostic final sera inclus dans votre dossier de candidature et servira de base de discussion dans le cadre des entretiens de sélection.

Vous trouverez plus d-informations ici.

The Registered Nurse (RN) in the Medical Surgical Day Unit (MSDU) provides comprehensive pre-operative and procedural nursing care for patients undergoing Interventional Radiology, MRI, and surgical procedures at the West Roxbury campus.

The RN also administers infusion therapies such as IVIG and may float to the Ambulatory Surgery Unit in Jamaica Plain as needed. This role requires strong clinical judgment, independent practice, and effective collaboration with interdisciplinary teams to ensure safe, high-quality patient care throughout all phases of the peri-procedural experience.

The RN serves as a patient advocate and supports clinical, administrative, educational, and research aspects of the service. Deliver comprehensive pre-operative and procedural nursing care for Operating Room, Interventional Radiology, and MRI patients.

Perform full nursing assessments; validate consents and H&P documentation; initiate IV access/venipuncture; and complete required pre-procedure testing. Verify accuracy of surgical site preparation, marking, and patient consent. Administer medications as ordered and monitor patient responses.

Provide clear pre-operative teaching and review discharge instructions with patients and families. Monitor post-operative patients recovering from anesthesia or sedation, assessing for side effects or complications. Maintain knowledge of ASPAN standards, VHA directives, and service-level SOPs.

Document all phases of care accurately and promptly in the electronic health record. Function independently and serve as Charge Nurse when assigned. Provide guidance and education to students and newly onboarded staff. Apply the nursing process to coordinate evidence-based, interdisciplinary care focused on health promotion and disease prevention.

Participate in quality-improvement initiatives to enhance patient care and workflow efficiency. Collaborate on patient-flow processes including Travel, Housing, and Chaperone coordination. Provide clinic coverage as assigned and maintain required procedural and core competencies.

Support patient care throughout the entire visit from check-in through discharge. Demonstrate strong communication skills and professional behaviors that support teamwork and collaboration with colleagues and patients. Work Schedule: Monday-Friday, 10:30 A.M.-7 P.M. or 9:30 A.M.-6 P.M.

Die Psychotherapie Tagesklinik (PTK) des Universitären Psychiatrischen Zentrums (UPZ) bietet eine spezialisierte Versorgung für psychisch belastete Menschen in schwierigen Lebensumständen. Sie richtet sich an Patient\*innen, für die eine ambulante Therapie nicht ausreicht, die jedoch keine stationäre Behandlung ötigen.

In der PTK werden insbesondere Menschen mit Depressionen, Angst\- und Zwangsstörungen, Persönlichkeitsstörungen sowie posttraumatischen Belastungsstörungen behandelt.

Der therapeutischen Arbeit in der PTK liegt ein vielschichtiges Behandlungskonzept zugrunde, das unterschiedliche psychotherapeutische Grundhaltungen sowie allgemeine störungsspezifische Wirkfaktoren der Psychotherapie integrativ kombiniert.

Das Therapieprogramm beinhaltet Elemente der kognitiven Verhaltenstherapie (KVT), u. a. der Dialektisch Behavioralen Therapie (DBT) sowie der emotionsfokussierten Therapie. Die Behandlung und Betreuung wird von einem engagierten, kollegialen Team gewährleistet, dem du sehr gerne selbst angehören kannst.

Die PTK bietet zudem geregelte Arbeitszeiten zu den üblichen Bürozeiten und damit für dich einen planbaren Arbeitsalltag.

Du sorgst für eine individuelle, professionelle Pflege und begleitest unsere Patientinnen und Patienten durch komplexe Genesungsprozesse
In akuten Krisensituationen agierst du souverän und mit Empathie – deine Ruhe und Fachkompetenz machen den Unterschied
Als Bezugsperson übernimmst du die Verantwortung für den gesamten Pflegeprozess und trägst massgeblich zur Kontinuität in der Therapie bei
Du leitest Patient\*innengruppen wie z. B. Achtsamkeit, Emotionsregulation, Skills, Sport etc.
Im interdisziplinären Team arbeitest du eng mit Fachkräften aus verschiedenen Disziplinen zusammen, um das bestmögliche Ergebnis für unsere Patientinnen und Patienten zu erreichen und um die Selbstwirksamkeit aktiv zu fördern

Auch in herausfordernden Situationen bleibst du ruhig und gelassen, zeigst Eigeninitiative und übernimmst Verantwortung

Performs comprehensive preoperative assessments, including review of medical history, medications, allergies, laboratory results, diagnostic studies, and surgical consent. Verifies patient identity, procedure, surgical site, allergies, and other required safety information in accordance with established perioperative safety standards.

Performs and documents the nursing assessment and develops an individualized plan of care based on the patient's condition and surgical needs. Functions as the circulating RN, maintaining responsibility for patient safety, aseptic technique, documentation, positioning, equipment, supplies, and coordination of the surgical environment.

May function as a scrub RN, assisting with sterile procedures, instrumentation, supplies, and surgical counts according to competency and facility requirements. Participates in surgical time-outs and other patient-safety processes to prevent wrong-patient, wrong-site, and wrong-procedure events.

Performs accurate counts of instruments, sharps, sponges, and other surgical items in collaboration with the surgical team. Maintains strict adherence to infection prevention and control practices, including sterile technique and appropriate handling of surgical instruments and specimens.

Handles, labels, and transports surgical specimens according to established policies and procedures. Administers medications and treatments within the RN's scope of practice and applicable VA policies.

Provides postoperative assessment and nursing care, including monitoring for complications and coordinating the patient's transition to the appropriate postoperative care area. Provides education to Veterans and families regarding surgical procedures, postoperative care, medications, wound care, and recovery instructions.

Recognizes and responds appropriately to emergency situations, including hemorrhage, cardiac or respiratory compromise, anaphylaxis, and other intraoperative complications. Participates in emergency and urgent surgical procedures as required.

Accurately documents nursing care, assessments, interventions, medications, surgical counts, specimens, and patient responses in the electronic health record. Collaborates with surgeons, anesthesia providers, surgical technologists, nursing staff, and other interdisciplinary team members to coordinate safe and effective patient care.

Participates in quality improvement, patient safety, infection prevention, and performance improvement activities within the Operating Room and Perioperative Service. Maintains current knowledge and competency in perioperative nursing practices, surgical procedures, equipment, infection prevention, and patient-safety standards.

Assists with orientation, training, and competency development of new staff and nursing students when assigned.
